children: Kyrgyzstan’s GDP expanded by 11.0% year-on-year in January–August 2026, easing from a four-month low of 11.1% growth recorded in January–July.

The services sector grew by 6.3%, down 3.6 percentage points from the previous period, and accounted for 49.2% of total GDP. The slowdown was mainly driven by weaker growth in the industry sector (8.8% vs 11.1%), mining (8.9% vs 16.9%), manufacturing industries (10.1% vs 11.8%), and hotel activities and restaurants (9.5% vs 9.6%).

On the other hand, goods-producing industries grew by 2.7% and accounted for 34.7% of GDP, lifted by gains in agriculture, forestry, and fishing (6.4% vs 6.0%), water supply, waste treatment, and recycling of raw materials (17.8% vs 17.3%), and construction (61.0% vs 60.6%).

title: Kyrgyzstan GDP Eases in January-August
